Example: QRISK3 cardiovascular risk model

Source: vignettes/qrisk3.Rmd
qrisk3.Rmd

This vignette shows modelscloud against a real deployed model: QRISK3, which estimates an individual’s 10-year risk of developing cardiovascular disease. It is served as resplab/qrisk3pexa, a wrapper around the QRISK3 R package.

Unlike the toy models in the Getting started vignette, this model lives outside the public examples collection, so you’ll need your own API key.

library(modelscloud)

connect_to_model("resplab/qrisk3pexa", access_key = "YOUR_API_KEY")

Sample input

QRISK3 takes a table of patients. get_sample_input() returns a ready-to-use example dataset (the QRISK3 package’s bundled test patients, with column names matching the model’s API):

patients <- get_sample_input()
head(patients)
#>   patid gender age atrial_fibrillation weight height ethiniciy ...
#> 1     1      1  64                   0     80    178         1 ...
#> 2     2      0  58                   1     72    165         1 ...

nrow(patients)
#> [1] 19

Pass n to get just the first few rows:

get_sample_input(n = 3)    # first 3 patients

Running the model

model_run() predicts every patient in the input and returns a data frame with the QRISK3 score columns added:

results <- model_run(patients)
head(results[, c("ID", "QRISK3_2017")])
#>   ID QRISK3_2017
#> 1  1    17.22985
#> 2  2    36.01234
#> 3  3     9.84512

Because the result is a native R data frame, you can summarise or plot it locally as usual:

summary(results$QRISK3_2017)
hist(results$QRISK3_2017,
     main = "Predicted 10-year CVD risk", xlab = "QRISK3 score (%)")

One-liner

get_sample_input() feeds straight into model_run():

results <- model_run(get_sample_input())

QRISK3 is a prediction model: every call is synchronous — model_run() returns the predictions directly. For a model that supports asynchronous execution, see the Example: EPIC-R vignette.
